description.narrative: TZOME IXUK, Mujeres Organizadas, A.C. is a cooperative of indigenous Tojolabal Ubia women in Chiapas, in the southeast of Mexico. For 25 years, the organization has been working to defend human rights and gender equality based on their experiences and knowledge as indigenous Tojolabal people. They provide legal advice; they provide shelter to women survivors of violence and migrants who face risks; and they create spaces for education and training. The organization has increased the offer of direct services due to the increase in migrant women arriving in Mexico (particularly from El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras).The grant will support the following specific priorities:- Offer women, their migrant daughters and sons, refugees and asylum seekers: food, spaces for training in their rights, shelter and spaces for healing from violence through ancestral Tojolabal knowledge;- Guarantee decent and fair salaries for the team;- Raise awareness and training of public servants who work directly with migrant women and their families;.- Strengthen participation in networks and alliances to defend the rights of people in migration contexts;- Raise awareness on issues related to the rights of migrants- Provide spaces for self-care and collective care.
